title: Practice Mirror Report Content
description: Structured content authored by the LLM (Claude Code) and consumed by analysis/render_report.py. Numbers come from metrics.json via *_ref fields — the LLM does not round-trip arithmetic.

schema_version.description: Lock to 1.0 in v3.0; bump when the contract breaks.

title.description: Title in 'The X Who Y' form. Archetype italicized in HTML; modifier upright. Both LLM-authored.

modifier.description: What makes THIS user specific within their archetype (e.g., 'Who Audits'). 1-3 words; sentence-case.

tagline.description: One short sentence under the title — a vivid character-line that captures the user in one breath. Reserve the longer thesis for the pullquote in Section I.

fingerprint_badge.description: Optional. Reserved for a future renderer. The current renderer does NOT show a percentile pill in the hero — the in-hero 2x2 communicates fingerprint sharpness spatially. Authors may omit; renderer ignores.

ref.description: Path into metrics.json that resolves to one of: 'sharp', 'typical', 'borderline'.

label_map.description: Map from sharpness value to display label.

score_ref.description: Path into metrics.json for the numeric score (rendered alongside the label).

headline_stats.description: Optional. Reserved for a future renderer to surface 1-3 high-level stats. The current renderer relies on the fingerprint_badge in the hero and the trait bars in Section I — the headline-stats row is dropped from v3.0 to keep the hero screenshot-tight. Authors may omit; renderer ignores.

shadow.description: Shadow archetype shown in the hero. tagline is LLM-authored prose; name and axis are refs into metrics.json so they always match the data layer.

section_identity.description: Section I — pure recognition, no deficits.

traits.description: Exactly three traits. Typical pattern is 2 high + 1 contrast, but 3 high is allowed when the data calls for it.

pullquote.description: The screenshot moment. One sentence (or two short ones) with weight; renderer applies serif-italic + paper-warm panel.

recognition_lines.description: 'You'll know this is you if…' lines. Second-person, behavior-specific, written for uncanny-recognition. Until research authors per-archetype lines, the LLM provides them inline.

section_outcome.description: Section II — where the data shows tension. Strengths alongside trade-offs; honest but not deficit-framed.

comparison_values.description: Cohort comparison rows for the gauge. value_static is allowed for cross-archetype facts (e.g., 'Reality Tester ships at 22.7%') because they're stable corpus statistics from archetype_baselines.csv, not user data.

section_moves.description: Section III — exactly two moves, each named as a borrow from another archetype.

compass.description: Spatial map placing the user among all 7 archetypes. Renderer computes coordinates from all_scores + sharpness; the content JSON only specifies whether to include it and which refs to read.

reflection_prompts_ref.description: Path into metrics.json that resolves to a list of 3 prompt strings. Authored by research; LLM only references them.

trait.description: A signature behavior with a friendly name, prose characterization (no numbers), and a data reference the renderer uses to draw the bar pair.

kind.description: Narrative role. 'high' = a defining strength; 'contrast' = an archetype-typical move you've replaced (framed positively, not as a deficit).

characterization.description: What the move looks like in human terms. NO numbers, NO percentile language — those go in the bar.

signal.description: Signal name. Renderer reads user_archetype.user_signal_rates[signal] for user value, user_archetype.within_archetype_positioning.signals[signal=X].cohort_p50 for cohort baseline.

kind.description: primary = the user's value (highlight color); cohort = comparison row (muted).

from_archetype.description: Full archetype name: 'The Reality Tester', 'The Pair Programmer', etc.

verb_phrase.description: Imperative move name with terminal punctuation: 'Run it yourself.', 'Reframe the goal mid-flight.'

body_lead.description: Why this move, given the user's data. One sentence.

body_action.description: What to actually do this week. Concrete, behavioral. May include backticks for inline code (e.g., `git diff`).

effect_size_signal.description: Optional signal name from signal_effect_sizes; renderer can pull the pp delta to ground the recommendation.

effect_size_note.description: Optional human-readable framing of the research correlate.
